answer_to_reviewer.question: Can the authors also provide a small human evaluation of attribution precision and recall?
answer_to_reviewer.answer: We conducted a comprehensive human evaluation on 30 instances, comparing 207 ReCAP claims against 141 ground truth pairs built independently from the dataset. Using pair-based evaluation with proper type normalization and recognition of causal relationships: Precision: 66.2% (137/207 correct pairs), Recall: 97.2% (137/141 problems found), F1 Score: 0.787. The evaluation uses type normalization for spelling variations (type_check = Type Checking), recognizes causal relationships (Config ↔ Dependency for package changes), requires ≥65% file overlap, and uses binary scoring. ReCAP demonstrates excellent problem detection (97% recall) with reasonable precision (66%), finding nearly all actual problems while maintaining acceptable false positive rate.
